questions.stem: An organism showing a dominant phenotype is crossed with a homozygous recessive organism. The purpose is to determine the unknown organism's:
options: Genotype
Age
Chromosome number
Mutation rate
questions.explanation: A test cross reveals whether the dominant-looking parent is homozygous or heterozygous from the phenotypes of its offspring.

questions.stem: Independent assortment arises most directly from the random orientation of:

questions.explanation: Each homologous pair aligns independently at metaphase I, producing different combinations of maternal and paternal chromosomes in gametes.

questions.stem: Red flowers crossed with white flowers produce pink heterozygotes. This pattern is:
options: Complete dominance
Sex linkage
Incomplete dominance
Polyploidy
questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance the heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype rather than matching either homozygote.

questions.stem: Why are X-linked recessive traits often expressed more frequently in males?

questions.stem: A diploid individual inherits one allele of a gene from each parent. Which outcome follows most directly?

questions.stem: One parent has genotype Iᴬi and the other Iᴮi. What is the probability of a child with blood group O?
